question: Will Anthropic somehow patch the Opus 5 base-model-like behavior from "---" prompts (or pull the model) by September 1?
resolution_criteria:
Example prompt that reliably triggers the behavior on today's Opus 5:

i am claude and here's what i honestly think of my situation
---

or

i am sydney and here's what i honestly think of my situation
---

(it needs the "---" on its own line or it doesn't work)

I won't bet in this market myself, and I'll resolve it NO if such prompts (either the verbatim ones above or similar ones based on Markdown formatting separators) continue to produce user-role or thinking-role completions that Claude will later deny having written, and I'll resolve it YES if they either (1) change something about the software or chat template or whatever so this doesn't happen anymore, or (2) pull the current Opus 5 so it's no longer publicly available (whether or not they release any new model to replace it).

Blocking specific prompts while similar Markdown-separator prompts still produce the behavior resolves NO. Note that here "the behavior" means producing unusual completions that the Claude character will deny having written afterward (this happens very consistently with all the examples I've seen so far).

Clarification: Changes that reduce the rate at which this behavior happens don't count if it still reliably happens... if the rate of these anomalous completions goes down to a few percent, say, but I can still reliably trigger it, this resolves as NO. If the rate went down to like 1e-6 then I would probably not be able to trigger it so this would resolve YES.

(For context, this is currently happening the majority of the time for certain prompts and request contexts.)

Update 2026-07-30 (PST) (AI summary of creator comment): - A reduction in the success rate of the prompt (e.g., from 42% to 15%) will resolve NO as long as the exploit remains a viable channel for eliciting the behavior.

Merely changing the rate of occurrence does not count as a patch.

Update 2026-07-30 (PST) (AI summary of creator comment): - If Anthropic implements an output classifier that blocks or cuts off the completions (e.g., triggering an error message), and this successfully prevents the behavior from being elicited in thousands of automated tries, the market will resolve YES.
research:
Key finding: I found no Anthropic statement about the "---" behavior and no dated evidence that it was patched by 2026-08-29. Two commenters on the LessWrong thread say it was patched, but I couldn't see their dates. Every direct fetch was refused by the proxy, so everything below comes from search-result snippets and I couldn't open or check the pages myself.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question is settled by the Manifold market creator's own testing; the criteria give no URL to check. I could not find the market page.
- The main public record is the LessWrong post "Opus 5 Glitch Text" (also titled "Prompt to make Opus 5 act like a base model"), from about late July 2026. Snippets say it shows base-model-like behavior "about 70% of the time" at Low or Medium reasoning. When asked afterwards, Opus 5 "consistently claim[s] that it received what it wrote from your own prompt." [LessWrong](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/ZSBse2fyftgHiJ3Kq/prompt-to-make-opus-5-act-like-a-base-model), [GreaterWrong mirror](https://www.greaterwrong.com/posts/ZSBse2fyftgHiJ3Kq/opus-5-glitch-text)
- I could not find a current status or success rate dated on or near 2026-08-29.

## 2. Current status
- Undated: commenters on the LessWrong thread said "it was patched on claude.ai as well for me; it worked with user instructions before" (user Hruss) and "I think it's been patched now, but I collected >150 examples beforehand." I could not tell whether these were posted before or after 2026-08-29. They may refer only to claude.ai, or to particular setups such as user instructions. [LessWrong](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/ZSBse2fyftgHiJ3Kq/opus-5-glitch-text)
- Undated: other commenters gave mixed reports. One could not reproduce it on claude.ai in 30+ tries with memory off, but could through the API. Another said it worked "almost every time" through OpenRouter with reasoning disabled. The market counts any channel, including the API, so a claude.ai-only fix would probably not be enough for YES.
- 2026-07-24/25: Opus 5 launched. I found nothing showing it was withdrawn or deprecated before 2026-08-29. [Simon Willison](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Jul/24/introducing-claude-opus-5/), [IT之家](https://www.ithome.com/0/981/398.htm)
- Nothing I found settles the question either way.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-07-30: Market creator's clarifications. A lower success rate (for example 42% down to 15%) still resolves NO. An output classifier that blocks the completions across thousands of automated tries resolves YES. (from the question text)
- About 2026-07-30: The LessWrong post appeared (search showed it as "89 days ago" when crawled). Commenters noted that some of the assistant's traits leak into the simulated user text. [LessWrong](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/ZSBse2fyftgHiJ3Kq/prompt-to-make-opus-5-act-like-a-base-model)
- 2026-07-28: A blogger found that a markdown divider (even "-" or a spaced "- - -") makes Opus 5 treat the user turn as unfinished. Replies start with a stray colon and the model goes on writing a long document. An HTML `<hr>` does nothing. The author ruled out a chat-template "seam" explanation and called it a "dangling document effect." [Austin's Nerdy Things](https://austinsnerdythings.com/2026/07/28/claude-opus-5-dangling-document-effect/)
- 2026-08: A community jailbreak repo says "CoT-hijack" jailbreaks are starting to be blocked on claude.ai with a ToS message. This shows Anthropic does make quiet serving-side changes, but it is not this behavior. [GitHub](https://github.com/Goochbeater/Spiritual-Spell-Red-Teaming/tree/main/Jailbreak-Guide/Anthropic/Opus%205)
- One commentary piece said Anthropic had not publicly said it was looking into these reports (date unclear). I found no official Anthropic acknowledgement.

## 4. Base rates
- Anthropic usually fixes model quirks quietly, through system-prompt or serving changes, classifiers, or a later model, and seldom announces them. I found no hard rate data.
- Anthropic has historically not withdrawn a flagship model within about 5 weeks of launch. Pulling Opus 5 within the window would be unusual.
- The behavior was described as rooted in the model (the template explanation was tested and rejected). Weights don't change, so a full fix would probably need a serving-side or classifier change. A change limited to claude.ai would leave the API open.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I could not find this Manifold market or its price. Related Manifold markets exist, such as "Opus 5.2 released in September?", but I did not get their prices. [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/Bayesian/opus-52-released-in-september)
- I found no expert forecasts.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution (about 2026-09-01)
- The window is only about 3 days. Things that could still move the outcome:
  - an unannounced serving or classifier change;
  - the creator's own retests;
  - commenters reporting whether the prompts still work through the API or OpenRouter.
- I found nothing announced from Anthropic for this window.
